dedupe_keys.name: china system dynamics cost benefit assessment of domestic waste management to 2100 under 80 scenarios

description: This case study builds a system dynamics model of China's domestic waste management system to assess its long-term costs and benefits. The authors, Chunyu Tu, Zhaoxia Guo and Qi Liu of Sichuan University, posted the work as a preprint on Research Square in May 2026 under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, free to read online. The model links waste generation, separation and treatment with socioeconomic drivers and with environmental and social outcomes. The authors ran 80 scenarios, combining 16 levels of waste separation with five demographic and economic trends, and assessed total, economic, social and environmental cost-benefit performance from 2025 to 2100. Coverage is national. Caveats: the preprint has not been peer reviewed, and results depend on assumed prices, technology and population paths. The authors report that achieving full separation of both recyclables and wet waste under the historical trend raises total cost-benefit substantially compared with the historical separation level, and they present the framework as a basis for waste and environmental policy in a circular economy. Simulation uses: long-run scenarios of separation policy for waste service capacity and investment models. Related records: the Chinese multi-city waste allocation framework (model-msw-optimization-multi-city-nsga2) and the COVID-19 medical waste study (case_study-china-covid19-medical-waste-343-cities) are related national analyses.
